exposure: number of ANC visits (No ANC visits)
cohort: The study included 283,785 reproductive-age women who had a short preceding birth interval across 21 Sub-Saharan African countries.
finding: One in ten women with short birth intervals in Sub-Saharan Africa experienced pregnancy termination, with individual factors (sex of preceding birth, maternal age, pregnancy complications, no ANC visits, previous cesarean section, short breastfeeding, traditional contraception, poor wealth) and urban residence significantly increasing the odds.
mod_finding: Previous cesarean section delivery was identified as an individual factor associated with higher odds of pregnancy termination (AOR = 1.74, 95% CI: 1.32, 2.30).
